title: Noor and the Compass
premise: Freya Fairweather, a bush pilot hauling medicine and gossip across the interior, owes a debt she can't name and carries a compass that belonged to the mother who abandoned her. When a dying prospector trades her a map to a forbidden river source for one promise — that his estranged daughter will learn what he found — Freya and Noor, the prospector's sharp-eyed granddaughter, fly into country no plane is cleared to enter. The glacier calving season opens the route upstream for only eleven days, and they are not the only ones chasing the source: a mining syndicate wants whatever the old man saw. Following the river on foot and by raft, Freya discovers the compass points not north but toward memory itself, revealing that her mother vanished into this same valley twenty years ago. At the source they find not treasure but a drowned town the syndicate flooded to bury its crimes — and Freya's mother, alive, keeping its record. In the end Freya chooses the found family in the boat over the power the compass offers, burns the map, and flies Noor home with the truth instead.
about_author: Freya Montrose spent six years as a floatplane dispatcher in the northern interior before turning to fiction, and her prose still smells faintly of avgas and spruce smoke. She writes adventure stories about people who owe debts to landscapes.

chapters.title: Cargo of Rumors
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Freya's POV. Freya lands at a dying airstrip town with medicine crates and gossip, establishing her debt to a fixer named Calloway and her habit of never staying anywhere. Emotional beat: restless competence masking rootlessness.

chapters.title: The Dying Prospector
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A prospector named Elias Vane stumbles off a ridge trail, frostbitten and shot, and trades Freya a greasecloth-wrapped map for a promise: tell my granddaughter Noor what I found at the river's source. Emotional beat: pity hardening into obligation.

chapters.title: Noor
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, first appearance. Seventeen, furious, working the cannery docks, Noor refuses to mourn the grandfather who left her family behind — until Freya shows her the map and the bullet hole story. Emotional beat: grief arriving as anger.

chapters.title: Calloway's Interest
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Calloway learns about the map through an informant and offers to forgive Freya's entire debt if she brings back whatever Vane found. She refuses; he smiles like a man holding collateral. Emotional beat: dread under bravado.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The pair plan the run: calving season opens the upper gorge for eleven days, then seals it. Noor insists on coming, over Freya's objections, and proves she can read water better than any pilot. Emotional beat: grudging partnership formed.

chapters.title: The Compass That Lies
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. On approach, Freya's inherited compass spins wildly near the valley mouth — pointing south, then at Noor. She hides it, unnerved, remembering her mother's disappearance. Emotional beat: the past tapping on the windshield.

chapters.title: Down in the Spruce
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Engine trouble forces a crash landing on a gravel bar; both survive, the plane does not. They salvage rafts, rope, and the medicine crate. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve — there is only forward now.

chapters.title: Syndicate Men
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A syndicate survey crew led by the courteous, ruthless Mr. Harkness finds their crash site and offers a ride downstream — meaning capture. The pair slip away at night through muskeg. Emotional beat: the hunt begins.

chapters.title: Rapids and Reckonings
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Running the first gorge by raft, Noor saves Freya from a wrap; afterward they finally trade stories — Vane's abandonment, Freya's mother, the debt. Emotional beat: walls down, trust earned in white water.

chapters.title: What the Compass Wants
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The compass drags them up a side channel to a cairn holding her mother's journal page: the compass was made here, it doesn't point north, it points to what you've lost. Emotional beat: vertigo of hope.

chapters.title: Harkness Closes In
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Syndicate boats appear behind them; a chase through fog ends with their raft holed and a night hiding in a bear den while searchlights sweep the banks. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Drowned Town
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They reach the reservoir behind the syndicate's dam and find rooftops under green water — a town bought, burned, and flooded to erase a massacre of striking miners. Vane was a witness, not a prospector. Emotional beat: horror reframing everything.

chapters.title: Halfway Point
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Midpoint crisis: Noor learns her grandfather helped build the dam before turning witness, and turns her fury on Freya for softening him. They split camps. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the loneliness of truth.

chapters.title: The Hermit of the Source
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. An old woman fishing the outflow feeds them and reveals herself: Maren Fairweather, Freya's mother, alive, keeper of the town's records and the compass's twin. Emotional beat: reunion as rupture — twenty years of silence.

chapters.title: Why She Stayed
chapters.summary: Maren's POV (one-off). Flashback chapter: how Maren found the drowned town, chose witnesshood over return, and let the compass choose her daughter. Emotional beat: love expressed as terrible absence.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Maren hands over the ledger of names — every person the syndicate erased. Noor reads her grandfather's confession inside it and forgives him posthumously. Emotional beat: grief resolved into purpose.

chapters.title: Harkness at the Dam
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Harkness takes Maren hostage at the dam house, demanding the ledger; Calloway arrives as his buyer, revealing the debt was always bait to flush the records out. Emotional beat: trap sprung, stakes absolute.

chapters.title: Calving Season
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The glacier calves early, flooding the gorge and cutting the syndicate's boats off. In the chaos Noor and Freya free Maren, but the ledger goes into the flood — except Noor memorized the names. Emotional beat: sacrifice and cunning.

chapters.title: What Power Offers
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Trapped with Harkness on the collapsing dam crest, Freya holds the compass, which offers her visions of everything she's lost — including a life where she stays powerful and safe. She chooses otherwise. Emotional beat: temptation refused.

chapters.title: The Crest Breaks
chapters.summary: Multiple POV, rapid cuts. Climax: the dam fails; Harkness drowns clutching salvage rights, Calloway flees, and Freya carries Maren out as the drowned town finally surfaces into daylight. Emotional beat: catharsis through destruction.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the ruined valley, Noor recites the ledger's names to the sky while survivors of the scattered town's descendants gather — the record survives in mouths, not paper. Emotional beat: mourning become memorial.

chapters.title: Flight Home
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Weeks later, Freya — debt settled, compass buried at the cairn — flies Noor and Maren to the coast to start over, then keeps flying, but now always with somewhere to land. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
